plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 (SiO2/Al2O3 multi-cavity UV bandpass) per feedback directives. Three complementary routes: (1) asymmetric cavity seed with expanded Bragg mirrors (29 layers), (2) same topology with global-then-local optimization to escape local minima, (3) alternative HfO2/SiO2 material system with identical asymmetric topology to test material sensitivity. All routes maintain parent_route_id='route_03' per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: Asymmetric cavity seed with expanded Bragg mirrors (29-layer SiO2/Al2O3)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Breaking the central cavity symmetry (layers 11-13 initialized at 66.0/67.5/69.0 nm instead of uniform 67.5 nm) while adding 2 period pairs to each Bragg mirror will enable the optimizer to redistribute spectral gain into sharper transition slopes, improving the target score beyond the 0.379 plateau observed in prior route_03 iterations.
routes.design_principle: 1-D photonic crystal filter with periodic main-function units sandwiched between anti-reflection coatings, following the SiO2/SiNx design methodology but adapted to SiO2/Al2O3 material pair for UV transparency.
routes.proposed_topology: 29 finite coating layers: [SiO2/Al2O3]_7 Bragg mirror | asymmetric 3-layer cavity (SiO2/Al2O3/SiO2) | [Al2O3/SiO2]_7 Bragg mirror, total 29 layers on fused silica substrate
design_variables: optimization bounds ±20% around quarter-wave at 267.5 nm
manufacturing_considerations: ALD or IAD recommended for thickness uniformity
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for periodic stack optimization
Asymmetric cavity initialization breaks optimization symmetry lock-in
Expanded Bragg mirror periods widen stopband bandwidth
expected_advantages: Wider stopband from additional mirror periods
Escaped local minimum from asymmetric seed
Improved transition sharpness between passband and stopband
known_risks: Increased layer count may amplify thickness tolerance sensitivity
Asymmetric seed may converge to different local minimum not necessarily better
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer SiO2/Al2O3 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate for solar-blind UV bandpass filtering. Layer sequence: alternating SiO2/Al2O3 starting with SiO2 (layer 1), total 29 finite layers. Initialize layers 1-10 as quarter-wave at 267.5 nm (SiO2 ~39 nm, Al2O3 ~67.5 nm), layers 11-13 as asymmetric cavity (66.0 nm SiO2, 67.5 nm Al2O3, 69.0 nm SiO2), layers 14-29 as alternating Al2O3/SiO2 quarter-wave. Optimization bounds: ±20% around initialization. Objective: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with coherent TMM solver. Air incidence, unpolarized or average of s/p. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Per feedback directive: break symmetry lock-in by seeding central cavity block (layers 11-13) with asymmetric profile (66.0/67.5/69.0 nm) instead of identical 67.5 nm; add 2 period pairs to Bragg mirrors (25→29 layers) to widen stopband and force optimizer to redistribute gain into sharper transition slopes.

routes.title: Global-then-local optimization on 29-layer asymmetric topology
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The 0.379 target score plateau in route_03 resulted from gradient optimizer converging to local minimum; a global search phase (differential evolution or particle swarm) followed by gradient refinement will discover superior thickness configurations on the same 29-layer asymmetric topology.
routes.design_principle: Same 29-layer SiO2/Al2O3 asymmetric cavity topology as route_03_refine_01, but with hybrid optimization strategy to explore broader thickness space before local refinement.
routes.proposed_topology: 29 finite coating layers: [SiO2/Al2O3]_7 Bragg mirror | asymmetric 3-layer cavity (SiO2/Al2O3/SiO2) | [Al2O3/SiO2]_7 Bragg mirror, total 29 layers on fused silica substrate
design_variables: optimization bounds ±25% around quarter-wave at 267.5 nm for global phase, then ±15% for local refinement
manufacturing_considerations: wider bounds may require tighter process control
theory_basis: Global optimization escapes local minima in multimodal thickness space
Transfer Matrix Method gradient refinement converges rapidly near optimum
Hybrid strategy balances exploration and exploitation
expected_advantages: Discovery of superior thickness configurations unreachable by gradient-only optimization
Validation that route_03 plateau was optimizer-limited rather than topology-limited
known_risks: Global search requires more function evaluations, may exceed computational budget
Wider bounds may produce candidates with impractical thicknesses
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer SiO2/Al2O3 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate using hybrid global-then-local optimization. Layer sequence identical to route_03_refine_01: alternating SiO2/Al2O3 starting with SiO2 (layer 1), 29 finite layers, asymmetric cavity initialization (layers 11-13: 66.0/67.5/69.0 nm). Phase 1: differential evolution or particle swarm with ±25% bounds, 500 evaluations. Phase 2: gradient-based refinement from best Phase 1 candidate with ±15% bounds, 200 evaluations. Objective: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. Use coherent TMM solver. Air incidence, unpolarized or average of s/p. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests whether route_03 plateau (0.379) was optimizer-limited rather than topology-limited. Same 29-layer asymmetric topology as route_03_refine_01 but with global search phase to escape local minima that gradient-only optimization cannot.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 material substitution on 29-layer asymmetric topology
routes.scientific_hypothesis: HfO2/SiO2 material pair provides higher refractive index contrast than SiO2/Al2O3 in the UV range, enabling wider stopband and sharper transitions with same 29-layer topology; target score should improve if index contrast is the limiting factor rather than layer count.
routes.design_principle: Same 29-layer asymmetric cavity topology as route_03_refine_01, substituting HfO2 (high-index) for Al2O3 while retaining SiO2 (low-index), leveraging HfO2 transparency and higher index in UV range.
routes.proposed_topology: 29 finite coating layers: [SiO2/HfO2]_7 Bragg mirror | asymmetric 3-layer cavity (SiO2/HfO2/SiO2) | [HfO2/SiO2]_7 Bragg mirror, total 29 layers on fused silica substrate
design_variables: optimization bounds ±20% around quarter-wave at 267.5 nm (SiO2 ~39 nm, HfO2 ~31 nm based on n~2.2)
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 requires ion-assisted deposition for moisture stability
HfO2 may exhibit inhomogeneity without IAD
theory_basis: Higher index contrast (HfO2 n~2.2 vs Al2O3 n~1.7) widens photonic stopband
HfO2/SiO2 demonstrated for UV long-pass edge filters with 90%+ transmission
IAD process reduces moisture-induced index shifts
expected_advantages: Wider stopband from higher index contrast
Potentially fewer layers needed for same rejection (future optimization)
Validates material sensitivity of route_03 topology
known_risks: HfO2 absorption edge may encroach on 255-280 nm passband
HfO2 inhomogeneity without IAD may cause thickness reproducibility issues
Material optical constants at 255-280 nm may differ from nominal values
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer HfO2/SiO2 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate for solar-blind UV bandpass filtering. Layer sequence: alternating SiO2/HfO2 starting with SiO2 (layer 1), total 29 finite layers. Initialize layers 1-10 as quarter-wave at 267.5 nm (SiO2 ~39 nm, HfO2 ~31 nm based on n~2.2), layers 11-13 as asymmetric cavity (38.0 nm SiO2, 31.0 nm HfO2, 40.0 nm SiO2), layers 14-29 as alternating HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave. Optimization bounds: ±20% around initialization. Objective: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with coherent TMM solver. Air incidence, unpolarized or average of s/p. Note: HfO2 requires ion-assisted deposition for UV transparency and moisture stability. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests material sensitivity of route_03 topology. Same 29-layer asymmetric topology but substitutes HfO2 for Al2O3 to leverage higher index contrast. If target score improves, index contrast was limiting factor; if score decreases, Al2O3 was superior for this UV bandpass application.
